front_blocks.md: Define **abstract data type (ADT)**.

back_blocks.md: An abstract data type is a **collection of data and a set of operations on that data**.

cards.front_md: Define **abstract data type (ADT)**.
cards.back_md: An abstract data type is a **collection of data and a set of operations on that data**.

front_blocks.md: Name three common abstract data types.

back_blocks.md: **Stacks**, **queues** and **linked lists**.

cards.front_md: Name three common abstract data types.
cards.back_md: **Stacks**, **queues** and **linked lists**.

front_blocks.md: Define **stack**.

back_blocks.md: A stack is an abstract data type that stores data using the **Last In, First Out (LIFO)** principle.

cards.front_md: Define **stack**.
cards.back_md: A stack is an abstract data type that stores data using the **Last In, First Out (LIFO)** principle.

front_blocks.md: What everyday object is a stack like?

back_blocks.md: **A pile of plates**: the last item you put on is the first one you take off.

cards.front_md: What everyday object is a stack like?
cards.back_md: **A pile of plates**: the last item you put on is the first one you take off.

front_blocks.md: What do PUSH and POP do?

back_blocks.md: **PUSH** adds an item to the **top** of the stack. **POP** removes the item from the **top**.

cards.front_md: What do PUSH and POP do?
cards.back_md: **PUSH** adds an item to the **top** of the stack. **POP** removes the item from the **top**.

front_blocks.md: Name the two pointers that a stack uses.

back_blocks.md: A **base pointer**, which points to the first item in the stack, and a **top pointer**, which points to the last item.

cards.front_md: Name the two pointers that a stack uses.
cards.back_md: A **base pointer**, which points to the first item in the stack, and a **top pointer**, which points to the last item.

front_blocks.md: What happens to the pointer when data is pushed onto a stack?

back_blocks.md: The pointer **increments by 1**, signifying the new top of the stack.

cards.front_md: What happens to the pointer when data is pushed onto a stack?
cards.back_md: The pointer **increments by 1**, signifying the new top of the stack.

front_blocks.md: What happens to the pointer when data is popped from a stack?

back_blocks.md: The pointer **decrements by 1**, to point at the new top of the stack.

cards.front_md: What happens to the pointer when data is popped from a stack?
cards.back_md: The pointer **decrements by 1**, to point at the new top of the stack.

front_blocks.md: Define **stack overflow**.

back_blocks.md: A stack overflow is an attempt to **push an item onto a full stack**.

cards.front_md: Define **stack overflow**.
cards.back_md: A stack overflow is an attempt to **push an item onto a full stack**.

front_blocks.md: Define **stack underflow**.

back_blocks.md: A stack underflow is an attempt to **pop an item from an empty stack**.

cards.front_md: Define **stack underflow**.
cards.back_md: A stack underflow is an attempt to **pop an item from an empty stack**.

front_blocks.md: What does `peek()` do on a stack?

back_blocks.md: It **returns the top value** of the stack without removing it, after first checking that the stack is not empty.

cards.front_md: What does `peek()` do on a stack?
cards.back_md: It **returns the top value** of the stack without removing it, after first checking that the stack is not empty.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Data that is popped is always erased from the stack.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
The data is **not necessarily erased**. The top pointer moves, and depending on the implementation the value may be deleted, replaced with a null value, or left to be overwritten.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Data that is popped is always erased from the stack.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

The data is **not necessarily erased**. The top pointer moves, and depending on the implementation the value may be deleted, replaced with a null value, or left to be overwritten.

front_blocks.md: Define **queue**.

back_blocks.md: A queue is an abstract data type that stores data **in the order it arrives**, using the **First In, First Out (FIFO)** principle.

cards.front_md: Define **queue**.
cards.back_md: A queue is an abstract data type that stores data **in the order it arrives**, using the **First In, First Out (FIFO)** principle.

front_blocks.md: What do ENQUEUE and DEQUEUE do?

back_blocks.md: **ENQUEUE** adds an item to the **back** of the queue. **DEQUEUE** removes the item from the **front**.

cards.front_md: What do ENQUEUE and DEQUEUE do?
cards.back_md: **ENQUEUE** adds an item to the **back** of the queue. **DEQUEUE** removes the item from the **front**.

front_blocks.md: What does `peek()` do on a queue?

back_blocks.md: It returns the value of the item at the **front** of the queue **without removing it** from the queue.

cards.front_md: What does `peek()` do on a queue?
cards.back_md: It returns the value of the item at the **front** of the queue **without removing it** from the queue.

front_blocks.md: Define **linear queue**.

back_blocks.md: A linear queue is a data structure that **consists of an array**, where items are added to the next available space and removed from the front.

cards.front_md: Define **linear queue**.
cards.back_md: A linear queue is a data structure that **consists of an array**, where items are added to the next available space and removed from the front.

front_blocks.md: What must be checked before adding an item to a linear queue?

back_blocks.md: That the **queue is not full**.

cards.front_md: What must be checked before adding an item to a linear queue?
cards.back_md: That the **queue is not full**.

front_blocks.md: Before removing an item from a queue you must make sure that the queue is not <u>**          **</u>.

back_blocks.md: Before removing an item from a queue you must make sure that the queue is not **empty**.

cards.front_md: Before removing an item from a queue you must make sure that the queue is not <u>**          **</u>.
cards.back_md: Before removing an item from a queue you must make sure that the queue is not **empty**.

front_blocks.md: What happens to the rear index pointer when an item is enqueued?

back_blocks.md: If the end of the array has not been reached, the **rear index pointer is incremented** and the new item is added to the queue.

cards.front_md: What happens to the rear index pointer when an item is enqueued?
cards.back_md: If the end of the array has not been reached, the **rear index pointer is incremented** and the new item is added to the queue.

front_blocks.md: What happens to the front pointer when an item is dequeued?

back_blocks.md: The item at the front of the queue is returned and the **front is incremented by 1**.

cards.front_md: What happens to the front pointer when an item is dequeued?
cards.back_md: The item at the front of the queue is returned and the **front is incremented by 1**.

front_blocks.md: Define **circular queue**.

back_blocks.md: A circular queue is a **static array with a fixed capacity** that **reuses the empty slots** at the front of the array which are freed when items are dequeued.

cards.front_md: Define **circular queue**.
cards.back_md: A circular queue is a **static array with a fixed capacity** that **reuses the empty slots** at the front of the array which are freed when items are dequeued.

front_blocks.md: Why is a circular queue used instead of a linear queue?

back_blocks.md: In a linear queue it would **take time to move items up to the start** of the array to free space at the end, so a circular queue **reuses the empty slots** instead.

cards.front_md: Why is a circular queue used instead of a linear queue?
cards.back_md: In a linear queue it would **take time to move items up to the start** of the array to free space at the end, so a circular queue **reuses the empty slots** instead.

front_blocks.md: When is a circular queue full?

back_blocks.md: When the **next position to be used is already occupied** by the item at the front of the queue.

cards.front_md: When is a circular queue full?
cards.back_md: When the **next position to be used is already occupied** by the item at the front of the queue.

front_blocks.md: What happens when the only item in a circular queue is dequeued?

back_blocks.md: The **rear and front pointers are reset**.

cards.front_md: What happens when the only item in a circular queue is dequeued?
cards.back_md: The **rear and front pointers are reset**.

front_blocks.md: Define **linked list**.

back_blocks.md: A linked list is an abstract data type where each item, or **node**, contains a **data field** and a **pointer to the next node** in the sequence.

cards.front_md: Define **linked list**.
cards.back_md: A linked list is an abstract data type where each item, or **node**, contains a **data field** and a **pointer to the next node** in the sequence.

front_blocks.md: What two things does each node in a linked list store?

back_blocks.md: The **actual data**, and a **pointer to the next item** in the list.

cards.front_md: What two things does each node in a linked list store?
cards.back_md: The **actual data**, and a **pointer to the next item** in the list.

front_blocks.md: In a linked list, the <u>**              **</u> field contains the address of the next item in the list.

back_blocks.md: In a linked list, the **pointer** field contains the address of the next item in the list.

cards.front_md: In a linked list, the <u>**              **</u> field contains the address of the next item in the list.
cards.back_md: In a linked list, the **pointer** field contains the address of the next item in the list.

front_blocks.md: Where are new items usually added in a linked list?

back_blocks.md: To the **start** of the list.

cards.front_md: Where are new items usually added in a linked list?
cards.back_md: To the **start** of the list.

front_blocks.md: What signals that the end of a linked list has been reached?

back_blocks.md: The **pointer field is empty or null**.

cards.front_md: What signals that the end of a linked list has been reached?
cards.back_md: The **pointer field is empty or null**.

front_blocks.md: How is a linked list traversed?

back_blocks.md: Check the list is not empty, start at the node the Start pointer points to, output the item at that node, then **follow the pointer to the next node**, repeating until the pointer field is empty.

cards.front_md: How is a linked list traversed?
cards.back_md: Check the list is not empty, start at the node the Start pointer points to, output the item at that node, then **follow the pointer to the next node**, repeating until the pointer field is empty.

front_blocks.md: When a node is added to a linked list, what happens to the node it follows?

back_blocks.md: The pointer field of that node is **updated to point to the new node**.

cards.front_md: When a node is added to a linked list, what happens to the node it follows?
cards.back_md: The pointer field of that node is **updated to point to the new node**.

front_blocks.md: How is a node removed from a linked list?

back_blocks.md: The pointer field of the **previous node is updated to bypass** the deleted node.

cards.front_md: How is a node removed from a linked list?
cards.back_md: The pointer field of the **previous node is updated to bypass** the deleted node.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A removed node is erased from the linked list.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
The node is **not truly removed**, it is only **ignored**. This is easier, but it wastes memory.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

A removed node is erased from the linked list.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

The node is **not truly removed**, it is only **ignored**. This is easier, but it wastes memory.

front_blocks.md: Give two disadvantages of a linked list compared with an array.

back_blocks.md: Storing pointers means **more memory is required**, and items can **only be traversed in sequence**, so an item **cannot be directly accessed** as it can in an array.

cards.front_md: Give two disadvantages of a linked list compared with an array.
cards.back_md: Storing pointers means **more memory is required**, and items can **only be traversed in sequence**, so an item **cannot be directly accessed** as it can in an array.
